Five years ago today, as the U.S. hurried to bring an end to its longest war
and Afghanistan's government collapsed, Taliban fighters
[swept](https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/august-15/kabul-falls-to-
taliban-us-withdrawal) into Kabul. The images were
[inescapable](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/aug/17/afghanistan-
striking-image-appears-to-show-640-people-fleeing-kabul-in-packed-us-military-
plane): desperate Afghans surrounding planes at Kabul airport, crowds pressed
against its gates, the last American military aircraft leaving.

Then, much of the world moved on.

But for Afghans, Aug. 15, 2021 was far from the end of the story. In the five
years since the Taliban recaptured power, hundreds of thousands promised
pathways to the U.S. have remained stranded; the Taliban has systematically
pushed women and girls out of public life; international aid has collapsed
while hunger has skyrocketed; millions of refugees have been forced back into
the country; and Afghanistan has once again become the center of major
regional conflict.

Here are seven things to know about Afghanistan, five years after the fall of
Kabul:

#### **1\. America evacuated more than 120,000 people. Hundreds of thousands
are still waiting**
